newsitem.title: USA: Ikon says Q3 and Q4 EPS below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Ikon says Q3 and Q4 EPS below estimates.

text.p: IKON Office Solutions Inc said Thursday its net earnings for its third and fourth quarters would be below analysts' estimates.

IKON said it expected to earn about $0.30 to $0.32 per share in the third quarter ending June 30, excluding $18 million to $22 million in business transformation costs. A First Call consensus of April 14 put earnings at $0.40 per share for the quarter.

IKON said it expected fourth-quarter earnings of about $0.33 to $0.36 per share, before transformation costs of about $20 million to $25 million. A First Call consensus put IKON's fourth-quarter earnings at $0.43 per share.
Company officials were not immediately available to elaborate on the projection, or to say how many cents per share the (pre-tax) transformation charges would amount to.
The company attributed the decline to short-term issues relating to its business transformation process, which it etimated will cost an additional $50 to $75 million in 1998.
"We failed to recognize the temporary strain the transformation would put on sales growth in our traditional copier business," said chief executive John Stuart in a statement.
He added Ikon expected to achieve 20 percent earnings growth in 1998 excluding the transformation costs.

Ikon said the transformation costs relate to consolidation of areas including consolidating purchasing, inventory control, logistics, and other activities. It said it would reduce the number of customer service centers in the United States.

The company attributed half of the projected operating shortfall in the third quarter to lower sales productivity in certain markets, which would result in a lower internal revenue growth rate of about 11 percent to 12 percent in North America.
The remainder Ikon attributed to sales, general and administrative expenses that it had expected to eliminate this quarter through the transformation process.
The company's stock slipped to 27-1/2 after the bell Thursday, down 4-1/2 from the unofficial close of 32.
